BusinessContext.Description: Critical migration from SWIFT MT103 (legacy format) to ISO 20022 pacs.008.001.08 (FIToFICustomerCreditTransfer). Part of the global SWIFT migration initiative where all MT messages will be replaced by MX (ISO 20022) by November 2025. MT103 is used for single customer credit transfers, while pacs.008 is its ISO 20022 equivalent with enhanced structured data, better compliance support, and richer remittance information capabilities.
BusinessContext.ApplicableDomains: Payments Hub, Treasury Operations, Corporate Banking, Retail Banking, Trade Finance, Compliance, AML Screening

General.ImpactIfFails: Message rejected - cannot process without unique identifier. Risk of duplicate payment if uniqueness not enforced.
General.BusinessRationale: Ensures end-to-end traceability across MT103 and pacs.008 systems. Critical for payment tracking, reconciliation, and investigations.
General.AuditRequirement: All message IDs must be logged with originating MT103 reference and conversion timestamp for minimum AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years per SOX compliance.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Unique message identification required per SWIFT Standards and ISO 20022 business rules. Duplicate prevention required per PSD2 Article 80.
General.DataPrivacy: Message ID itself is not PII. No GDPR special handling required for this field.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 20 is 16 chars max, pacs.008 MsgId is 35 chars max. Direct trim and copy - both formats are compatible without transformation.
General.CachingStrategy: Processed message IDs cached in Redis for DUPLICATE_DETECTION_WINDOW_DAYS days to enable fast duplicate detection without full database scan.

Condition.ElseAction: N/A
CONVERT_TO_UTC before setting field

General.ImpactIfFails: Message rejected by receiving system due to missing mandatory header field.
General.BusinessRationale: ISO 20022 requires precise creation timestamp for message ordering, replay detection, and SLA measurement. MT103 has no equivalent field - SWIFT FIN network handles its own timestamps.
General.AuditRequirement: Conversion timestamp logged alongside original MT103 reception time to measure processing latency per SLA monitoring.
General.ComplianceRequirement: ISO 20022 XML schema validation will reject message if CreDtTm is absent or malformed. UTC timezone required for cross-border consistency.
General.DataPrivacy: Timestamp is operational metadata. No PII. No GDPR restrictions.
General.MigrationNote: New mandatory field in ISO 20022 with no MT103 equivalent. Must be generated at conversion time. Always UTC (Z suffix) for consistency across time zones and DST changes.
General.CachingStrategy: Not applicable - timestamp must always reflect actual conversion moment.

Condition.ElseAction: N/A

Variable.description: MT103 always carries exactly one transaction - static constant

General.ImpactIfFails: ISO 20022 schema validation failure - NbOfTxs is mandatory in pacs.008 group header.
General.BusinessRationale: MT103 represents a single customer credit transfer by definition. pacs.008 supports batches but MT103 migration always produces count of 1. Required for schema compliance and downstream batch reconciliation.
General.AuditRequirement: No specific audit requirement for this field beyond standard message logging.
General.ComplianceRequirement: ISO 20022 pacs.008 schema requires NbOfTxs to equal the actual number of CdtTrfTxInf blocks. Always 1 for MT103 conversions.
General.DataPrivacy: Not applicable - count field contains no personal data.
General.MigrationNote: MT202 bulk (batch) to pacs.008 conversion would require dynamic count. For MT103 one-to-one conversion always hardcoded to 1.

REJECT with error "Invalid field 32A format - expected YYMMDDCCCNNNNN,NN"
REJECT with error "Invalid or unsupported currency code"
REJECT with error "Amount out of valid range (must be > 0 and <= MAX_AMOUNT)"
ROUND to MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES decimal places AND LOG warning
FLAG for AML compliance review AND PROCEED

General.ImpactIfFails: Payment cannot be executed. Wrong amount credited to beneficiary causes financial loss and potential legal liability.
General.BusinessRationale: Core financial value of the transaction. Any parsing or rounding error directly impacts the amount credited or debited. Basis for all downstream calculations including fees, FX, and GL posting.
General.PerformanceImpact: LOW (string parsing and decimal conversion - no external service call)
General.AuditRequirement: All amount conversions must be logged with original MT103 value (comma decimal) and converted value (dot decimal) per SOX financial controls. Amounts above LARGE_AMOUNT_THRESHOLD must generate AML alert log entry.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Amounts above LARGE_AMOUNT_THRESHOLD (10 000 EUR) must be flagged per EU 4th AML Directive Article 11. Currency must be on approved list per sanctions regulations.
General.DataPrivacy: Transaction amount is not PII under GDPR. However combined with account data it becomes sensitive - access restricted to authorized payment processing roles.
General.MigrationNote: CRITICAL FORMAT DIFFERENCE: SWIFT uses comma as decimal separator (25000,00). ISO 20022 uses dot as decimal separator (25000.00). This conversion is mandatory and must never be skipped. Amount precision is always 2 decimal places for major currencies.
General.CachingStrategy: No caching - amount must always be read directly from source message.

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Missing mandatory field 50K - ordering customer required"
REJECT with error "Cannot extract debtor name from field 50K"
TRUNCATE to 140 characters AND LOG warning with original value
BLOCK message AND ALERT compliance team immediately
FLAG for enhanced due diligence review AND PROCEED with hold

Variable.description: SEPA zone payments require IBAN for debtor account

General.ImpactIfFails: Payment rejected. Serious compliance violation if sanctioned entity not detected, or reconciliation failure if account not extracted.
General.BusinessRationale: Identity of the payer (name) is mandatory for AML/KYC compliance and sanctions screening. Account identification is required for debit reconciliation and SEPA compliance. Both are extracted from the same MT103 field 50K, which combines account + name + address in one free-text block.
General.PerformanceImpact: MEDIUM - text parsing is fast but sanctions screening API call adds 50-200ms latency.
General.AuditRequirement: Sanctions/PEP screening results and account number logged for AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years. Required by EU 4th AML Directive Article 40.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Mandatory real-time sanctions screening per OFAC/EU/UN lists. SEPA Regulation 260/2012 mandates IBAN for EUR payments within SEPA zone.
General.DataPrivacy: Debtor name and account number are PII under GDPR Article 4. Must be encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3).
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 50K combines account + name + address in free text format. ISO 20022 separates these into distinct structured elements (Dbtr/Nm, DbtrAcct/Id/IBAN or Othr/Id). firstLine() returns the name; accountLine() extracts and strips the optional /account prefix from the first line.
General.CachingStrategy: Sanctions list cached and refreshed every 4 hours. Account number never cached.

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Cannot determine debtor agent - field 52A absent and no sender BIC in header"
REJECT with error "Invalid BIC format - must be 8 or 11 alphanumeric characters"
LOG_WARNING "BIC not found in SWIFT directory" AND PROCEED - may be valid non-SWIFT institution
BLOCK message AND ALERT compliance team

General.ImpactIfFails: Payment routing failure - cannot identify institution responsible for debiting ordering customer. Correspondent banking chain broken.
General.BusinessRationale: Identifies the financial institution that will debit the ordering customer account. Essential for interbank settlement routing, correspondent banking chain, and compliance traceability.
General.PerformanceImpact: LOW - BIC validation is in-memory. Directory lookup served from cache (BIC_CACHE_TTL_HOURS hour TTL). Sanctions check adds 10-50ms.
General.AuditRequirement: BIC of debtor agent must be stored with transaction for FATF Travel Rule compliance. Required for correspondent banking audit trail.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Institution-level sanctions screening required per OFAC and EU regulations. BIC must not belong to sanctioned correspondent bank.
General.DataPrivacy: BIC codes are public identifiers - not PII under GDPR. No special data protection measures required.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 52A is optional. extractBIC() helper strips the optional /account prefix line. Best practice fallback is to use sender BIC from SWIFT message application header (block 1) as debtor agent when field absent.
General.CachingStrategy: SWIFT BIC directory cached in memory and refreshed every BIC_CACHE_TTL_HOURS hours. Reduces latency from ~50ms (API call) to under 1ms (memory lookup).

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Missing mandatory field 57A - creditor agent required for routing"
REJECT with error "Invalid BIC format in field 57A"
REJECT with error "Beneficiary bank BIC not reachable via SWIFT network"

General.ImpactIfFails: Payment cannot be delivered to beneficiary. Funds stuck in transit. Customer complaint and potential SLA breach.
General.BusinessRationale: Identifies the financial institution that will credit the beneficiary account. Absolutely critical for payment routing and delivery. Without this, payment has no destination.
General.PerformanceImpact: LOW - BIC validation and reachability check served from BIC_CACHE_TTL_HOURS hour cache.
General.AuditRequirement: Creditor agent BIC stored for end-to-end payment traceability and correspondent banking reconciliation.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Reachability verification prevents payments to non-SWIFT institutions. Sanctions check against beneficiary bank required per OFAC and EU regulations.
General.DataPrivacy: BIC is public identifier. No GDPR restrictions.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 57A maps directly to CdtrAgt in pacs.008. Field is mandatory in practice even though technically optional in schema - most receiving banks reject without it.
General.CachingStrategy: BIC reachability data cached with BIC_CACHE_TTL_HOURS hour TTL. SWIFT connectivity status refreshed from SWIFT Alliance Gateway every hour.

General.ImpactIfFails: Payment blocked or credited to wrong account. Compliance violation if sanctioned beneficiary not detected. Financial crime facilitation risk, or financial loss/customer dispute from misposted payment.
General.BusinessRationale: Identity of the payee (name) is critical for sanctions screening, fraud detection, and FATF Travel Rule compliance. Destination account (IBAN) is essential for correct funds crediting and SEPA compliance. Both extracted from the same MT103 field 59.
General.PerformanceImpact: MEDIUM - text extraction fast but sanctions API adds 50-200ms, IBAN checksum and account status check add further latency.
General.AuditRequirement: Beneficiary name, sanctions result, and account number logged for AUDIT_RETENTION_YEARS years. Mandatory per EU 4th AML Directive and FATF Travel Rule Recommendation 16.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Real-time sanctions screening mandatory. SEPA Regulation 260/2012 mandates IBAN for EUR payments within SEPA zone.
General.DataPrivacy: Creditor name and account number are PII under GDPR. Same protections as ordering customer: encrypted storage, access logging, retention exemption for AML records per GDPR Article 17(3)(b).
General.MigrationNote: Same combined extraction logic as ordering customer (MAPPING_05) but applied to field 59. Both fields share identical format: optional /account on first line followed by name and address lines.
General.CachingStrategy: Sanctions list cached, refreshed every 4 hours. Account validation results not cached.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional
TRUNCATE to REMITTANCE_MAX_LENGTH characters AND LOG warning with original length
FLAG for AML compliance review AND PROCEED

General.ImpactIfFails: Loss of payment purpose information. Customer reconciliation failure. Invoice matching impossible for accounts payable automation.
General.BusinessRationale: Provides context for payment purpose critical for invoice matching, accounts payable automation, and regulatory reporting. Also screened for AML suspicious keywords (weapon, narco, etc.).
General.PerformanceImpact: NEGLIGIBLE (string manipulation only - no external calls)
General.AuditRequirement: Remittance text logged with transaction for reconciliation audit trail. AML keyword flags logged separately with compliance alert.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Remittance information screened for AML suspicious patterns per bank AML policy. Some jurisdictions require structured remittance (ISO 11649 creditor reference) for regulatory reporting.
General.DataPrivacy: Remittance text may contain personal references (invoice to John Doe, etc.) making it potentially PII. Treat with same protections as name fields.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 70 is unstructured free text (4 lines x 35 chars = 140 chars total). joinLines() merges the multi-line field into one string; truncate(140) enforces the ISO 20022 Ustrd max length.
General.CachingStrategy: No caching required - pure text transformation.

Condition.ElseAction: USE_DEFAULT ("OTHR") AND LOG for manual review
USE_GENERIC_CODE ("OTHR") AND LOG for potential manual classification

Condition.Action: ENSURE_PURPOSE_SET with derived or default value
Condition.ElseAction: OPTIONAL - field may be left empty for non-requiring destinations

Variable.description: Comma-separated ISO country codes where purpose code is mandatory for cross-border payments

Variable.name: KEYWORD_MAP_VERSION
Variable.description: Version of the keyword-to-purpose-code mapping table in use

General.ImpactIfFails: Payments to countries requiring purpose code (China, India, Russia, Brazil) may be rejected by receiving bank. Statistical reporting to central bank incomplete.
General.BusinessRationale: Purpose codes enable central bank statistical reporting, regulatory compliance for capital controls, automated routing rules in treasury systems, and tax reporting. Mandatory in several jurisdictions.
General.PerformanceImpact: LOW (keyword search in remittance field - in-memory string operations only)
General.AuditRequirement: Derived purpose code logged with confidence score and derivation method for quality monitoring. Allows retroactive correction if keyword model updated.
General.ComplianceRequirement: China PBOC requires purpose code for all inbound cross-border payments. India RBI requires for certain transaction types. Brazil Bacen requires for regulatory reporting. EU/US optional but strongly recommended for STP.
General.DataPrivacy: Purpose code itself is not PII. Derived from remittance which may contain PII references - derivation process does not store remittance content separately.
General.MigrationNote: MAJOR CHALLENGE: Purpose code does not exist in MT103. purposeCodeMapping() derives it entirely from field 23B (bank operation code) and keyword analysis of field 70 (free text). Derivation accuracy typically 60-80%. Manual override workflow recommended for high-value transactions to PURPOSE_CODE_REQUIRED_COUNTRIES.
General.CachingStrategy: Keyword lookup table (KEYWORD_MAP_VERSION) loaded at startup and cached in memory. No per-transaction caching needed.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional

General.BusinessRationale: Field 53A identifies the sender's correspondent bank in the payment routing chain, required when the sender doesn't have a direct account relationship with the receiver.
General.AuditRequirement: Correspondent BIC logged as part of the full routing chain audit trail.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Full routing chain transparency required for correspondent banking due diligence (FATF Recommendation 16).
General.DataPrivacy: BIC is an institution identifier, not PII.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 53A maps to PrvsInstgAgt1 in pacs.008's payment chain, matching the standard SWIFT MT-ISO20022 crosswalk.
General.CachingStrategy: No caching - direct extraction from source field.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null

General.BusinessRationale: Field 54A identifies the receiver's correspondent bank, required when the receiver doesn't have a direct account relationship with the sender.
General.AuditRequirement: Correspondent BIC logged as part of the full routing chain audit trail.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Full routing chain transparency required for correspondent banking due diligence (FATF Recommendation 16).
General.DataPrivacy: BIC is an institution identifier, not PII.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 54A maps to InstdAgt in pacs.008's payment chain, matching the standard SWIFT MT-ISO20022 crosswalk.
General.CachingStrategy: No caching - direct extraction from source field.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional

General.BusinessRationale: Field 56A identifies an intermediary institution between the sender's and receiver's correspondents, used in more complex multi-hop routing chains.
General.AuditRequirement: Intermediary BIC logged as part of the full routing chain audit trail.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Full routing chain transparency required for correspondent banking due diligence (FATF Recommendation 16).
General.DataPrivacy: BIC is an institution identifier, not PII.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 56A maps to IntrmyAgt1 in pacs.008 — the same element used by MT202's :56A: mapping in MT202_to_pacs009.xml for consistency.

Condition.ElseAction: REJECT with error "Missing mandatory field 71A"
REJECT with error "Invalid charge bearer code in field 71A"

General.ImpactIfFails: Charge allocation dispute between debtor and creditor bank — direct financial impact.
General.BusinessRationale: Field 71A specifies which party bears transaction charges (SHA/OUR/BEN), a mandatory field with direct financial consequences that must map exactly to its ISO 20022 equivalent code.
General.AuditRequirement: Charge bearer code logged for billing reconciliation and dispute resolution.
General.ComplianceRequirement: SWIFT/ISO 20022 code crosswalk is fixed and non-negotiable: SHA→SHAR, OUR→DEBT, BEN→CRED.
General.DataPrivacy: Charge bearer code is not PII.
General.MigrationNote: MT103's 3-letter codes (SHA/OUR/BEN) map to pacs.008's ChargeBearerType1Code 4-letter codes (SHAR/DEBT/CRED) — NOT a 1:1 rename, the semantics also shift slightly (e.g. "OUR" = all charges to debtor = "DEBT").

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional

General.ImpactIfFails: Loss of free-text routing instructions intended for the next agent in the chain.
General.BusinessRationale: Field 72 carries free-text sender-to-receiver instructions (e.g. "/BNF/...", "/INS/...") that downstream agents in the payment chain may need to act on.
General.AuditRequirement: Free-text instructions logged with the transaction for audit trail.
General.DataPrivacy: May contain operational references; treat with same care as other free-text fields.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 72 is unstructured free text (6 lines x 35 chars = 210 chars); truncated to 140 chars to fit InstrForNxtAgt/InstrInf's ISO 20022 max length (some structured codewords like /INS/, /BNF/ may be lost — acceptable since they're advisory, not the primary payment instruction).
General.CachingStrategy: No caching required - pure text transformation.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional

General.ImpactIfFails: Receiver bank loses a processing instruction (e.g. same-day value, phone advice) it was supposed to act on.
General.BusinessRationale: Field 23E carries a coded instruction (SDVA, INTC, PHOB, TELB, HOLD, CHQB, ...) that the creditor's agent must honor.
General.AuditRequirement: Instruction code logged with the transaction.
General.ComplianceRequirement: None specific — operational instruction, not regulatory.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 23E may repeat up to 3 times in the real standard; this mapping only carries the first occurrence — acceptable since the dataset's parser captures a single value per field.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional

General.ImpactIfFails: Beneficiary cannot see the originally instructed amount before currency conversion — reconciliation discrepancy risk.
General.BusinessRationale: Field 33B carries the original currency/amount instructed by the ordering customer, distinct from the :32A: settlement amount when a currency conversion occurs en route.
General.AuditRequirement: Original instructed amount logged alongside the settlement amount for reconciliation.
General.DataPrivacy: Amount is transaction data, not PII.
General.MigrationNote: Maps to pacs.008's EqvtAmt (Equivalent Amount), the ISO 20022 element for an instructed amount expressed in a currency different from the interbank settlement currency.
General.CachingStrategy: No caching - direct extraction from source field.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional, only present when :33B: currency differs from :32A: currency

General.ImpactIfFails: Loss of the exchange rate used for the currency conversion — reconciliation and dispute-resolution impact.
General.BusinessRationale: Field 36 records the exchange rate applied when the instructed currency (:33B:) differs from the settlement currency (:32A:).
General.AuditRequirement: Exchange rate logged for reconciliation and audit of currency conversion.
General.MigrationNote: MT103's comma decimal separator is normalized to a dot to match ISO 20022 numeric conventions.

Condition.Action: PROCESS if present, skip if null
Condition.ElseAction: N/A - field is optional

General.ImpactIfFails: Loss of regulatory reporting information required by the ordering or beneficiary jurisdiction — potential compliance breach.
General.BusinessRationale: Field 77B carries statutory/regulatory reporting codes (e.g. /ORDERRES/, /BENEFRES/) mandated by certain jurisdictions' capital control or reporting regimes.
General.AuditRequirement: Regulatory reporting text logged with the transaction for compliance audit.
General.ComplianceRequirement: Required by jurisdictions enforcing balance-of-payments or capital-control reporting (e.g. France, Germany, Brazil).
General.DataPrivacy: May reference the ordering/beneficiary's country of residence; treat with same care as other regulatory fields.
General.MigrationNote: MT103 field 77B is free text (3 lines x 35 chars = 105 chars); this simplified mapping targets a single Inf leaf rather than pacs.008's full repeatable RgltryRptg/Dtls structure (Authrty/Ctry/Cd breakdown), consistent with this file's existing simplification of other free-text fields (e.g. RmtInf/Ustrd).
General.CachingStrategy: No caching required - pure text transformation.
